SOAP Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint: Severe left-sided throbbing headache since midday (several hours ago) with nausea and two episodes of vomiting; worsens with head/neck movement; preceded by zig-zag visual aura and transient blurred vision in both eyes; associated photophobia.
- Timeline: Similar episode a few weeks ago that lasted ~2 days and improved with rest and analgesics.
- Negative ROS: No fever, rash, speech disturbance, limb weakness/numbness, balance/coordination problems, head trauma, or breathlessness.
- Past medical history: Denies any chronic illnesses; no prior migraine diagnosis.
- Family history: Mother with migraines and hypothyroidism; no family history of brain tumors reported.
- Medications: Microgynon (combined oral contraceptive), dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Social history: Works in fashion industry; high job stress; lives alone; denies tobacco use and alcohol; minimal exercise.
- Allergies: Not documented.

Objective:
- No physical examination findings or vitals documented.
- No investigations performed or available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache
   - Assessment: Likely migraine with aura.
   - Differential diagnosis: Tension-type headache, cluster headache, secondary causes (e.g., intracranial mass) considered but less likely given history and lack of red-flag features.
   - Treatment planned: 
     • Simple and combination analgesics (Paracetamol, Co-codamol – dose/route/frequency not documented).  
     • NSAIDs (Ibuprofen or Naproxen – dose/route/frequency not documented).  
   - Patient education: Explanation of migraine nature, low likelihood of brain tumor; advised to maintain headache diary to identify triggers.
   - Safety-net advice: Return urgently if headaches worsen, persist >2–3 days, fail to respond to medication, or if neurological symptoms (weakness, visual changes, speech difficulty) or worsening neck pain develop.
   - Follow-up: Review next week to reassess frequency and discuss possible prophylactic therapy.

2. Health anxiety regarding brain tumor
   - Assessment: Cancer worry secondary to headache.
   - Treatment/Advice: Reassurance provided after assessment; encouraged to monitor symptoms and seek review if red-flag signs appear.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: Allergies, full medication reconciliation (OTC drugs, supplements), vital signs, physical examination details.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear dialogue; occasional minor overlaps but clinically adequate information.
